title: Sheinbaum Accuses AI and ‘Bots’ of Creating False Trends Against Her Administration
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [August 24, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/sheinbaum-acusa-uso-de-
ia-y-bots-para-crear-tendencias-falsas-contra-su-administracion), an
independent Mexican investigative magazine._

The **advance of artificial intelligence** has made it easier for conservative
actors with financial resources to **manufacture artificial trends on social
media** to discredit people or governments without any basis, President
**Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo** warned during her morning press conference.

Figures that appear to show millions of views, or of people talking about a
topic, in reality come from bots that, through artificial intelligence
mechanisms, **produce content at high speed and with no real human
involvement** , the president explained.

> They are not people, they are robots.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

She maintained that these tools have been **used for political ends** ,
particularly against humanist governments; as an example, the president cited
what has happened in various recent electoral processes in **Latin America**.

In response, she laid out two lines of action: the **dissemination of truthful
information** and a **push for regulation** that would keep digital platforms
from becoming a space where, she said, "the citizen" ends up displaced by
algorithmic manipulation.

Regarding the use of terms such as "narco-candidate," "narco-president," and
"narco-government" that were spread without any basis starting in her campaign
period, Claudia Sheinbaum recalled that it was an operation with a **component
of hypocrisy** , since proven ties between organized crime and PAN
administrations existed, in particular that of **Felipe Calderón** , in
reference to the case of the then Secretary of Public Security, **Genaro
García Luna**. "Now they dare to talk about something that has no basis
whatsoever."

She stressed that **any allegation of ties between a ruler and organized crime
must be backed by solid proof** and not by media accusations, and that it
would fall to the prosecutor's offices to investigate them. **" There has to
be proof, not announcements, not opinions,"** she underscored, and she
recalled that **Morena proposed in Congress** the **creation of a commission**
of the **National Electoral Institute** to **vet the candidates** in
coordination with the security agencies and the Attorney General's Office—a
**proposal that was rejected by the opposition parties**.

In that sense, the president questioned the **hypocrisy of the right and of
conservatism**. "Which government had ties to a criminal group? Calderón's […]
But now they are the ones dressing up as saints or moralists."

A right-wing government could hardly consolidate itself in the short term in
Mexico, President Sheinbaum ruled out, considering that these political forces
answer to "elite interests" foreign to the well-being of the population.

The country is doing well, the president insisted, pointing to the economic
indicators as backing and calling on citizens to stay informed in the face of
attempts to use fake news against governments. "We have to inform, inform,
inform, inform," so that **citizens can tell the difference between real data
and digital manipulation**.
